questions.q: I'm running cold Meta traffic to an advertorial before the product page. What click-through rate from the advertorial to the PDP should I be aiming for before I decide the page is broken?
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/$100 Million Advertorial Formula.txt
questions.quote: you want about 30% of people to to click through uh ideally even like 40% to the second page
answer_points: About 30% of advertorial readers should click through to the next page (the PDP)
Ideally up to 40%

questions.q: How do I pick which kind of advertorial to write? Some of my buyers just don't trust us, others seem to want someone to tell them it's OK to buy.
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/$100 Million Advertorial Formula.txt
questions.quote: obstacle is a low trust for your product, then you need the story plus proof early in the advertorial
answer_points: Match the format to the main obstacle: low trust -> storytelling format with proof early
Needing permission -> authority/expert format (e.g. a doctor or vet)
Skepticism or too many options -> buyer's guide / comparison listicle; "will it work for me" -> case study

questions.q: What share of people who start my product quiz should make it all the way through to the sales page?
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/how i build quiz funnels that make $1,073,966_mo with branded dropshipping.txt
questions.quote: The target completion rate that you should be aiming for approximately 30%.
answer_points: Target about 30% completion of quiz starters
Around 25% is still acceptable at scale

questions.q: My landing page gets around 15,000 visitors a month. Is it worth setting up A/B tests on it yet?
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/The Only Landing Page Guide You_ll Ever Need.txt
questions.quote: if you're under 25,000 to 30,000 visitors a month, like I said earlier in the video, you do not want
answer_points: No: below roughly 25,000-30,000 monthly visitors A/B tests take too long and will not reach significance
Use qualitative research instead (user testing such as UserBrain plus Clarity recordings)

questions.q: My Meta ad is already a long 2,000-word story. Should the advertorial it clicks through to be long as well?
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/How I build $1k_day advertorials with Claude in 6 minutes and 41 seconds.txt
questions.quote: you might want to try a more direct advertorial where you cut to the product a lot sooner
answer_points: If the ad does heavy selling (long copy or VSL), make the advertorial shorter and show the product sooner
If the ad does little selling (e.g. a clickbait image), the advertorial must be long and do the selling

questions.q: I want to pop a 'what's stopping you from buying?' survey on my product page. When in the visit should it fire?
questions.source: 07-LPG-landing-pages/The BEST Conversion Rate Optimization Tutorial for Ecommerce in 2025.txt
questions.quote: you basically want to time it to be roughly around 60% of your average session duration
answer_points: Fire it at about 60% of the average session duration (e.g. around 1 minute if sessions average 2 minutes)
Ask an open-ended question about what is holding them back from buying

questions.q: Shopify says my average order is about $70, but carts are all over the place. Should I set my free-gift threshold just above that average?
questions.source: 03-OFF-offers/How 8 and 9 Figure Brands Build Offers Without Discounting.txt
questions.quote: look at the distribution curve, not look at any averages, and then build an offer around the two peaks
answer_points: Do not set thresholds off the mean AOV when the order-value distribution has two peaks
Look at the distribution and build a separate threshold offer just above each peak

questions.q: For my subscription brand, should I put effort into lifting month-3 retention with gifts, or into getting more first-time buyers to choose subscribe?
questions.source: 03-OFF-offers/The Most Valuable Subscription Video You_ll Watch in 2026 _ Ft. Matthew Holman (1).txt
questions.quote: I can go from a 40% subscriber opt-in rate to 45% subscriber opt-in rate
answer_points: Prioritise the first-order subscription opt-in rate (an acquisition problem), e.g. testing offers to move opt-in from 40% to 45%
Retention tweaks are capped and take months to show results

questions.q: On my product page, should one-time purchase or subscription be the option that is ticked when the page loads?
questions.source: 03-OFF-offers/The $100M Subscription Brand Playbook.txt
questions.quote: The first big no no is that the one-time purchase is automatically selected.
answer_points: Pre-select the subscription option, never the one-time purchase
People bias toward the default, and first orders on subscription carry higher LTV

questions.q: For my welcome pop-up, should the offer be a flat amount off or a percentage off?
questions.source: 03-OFF-offers/I Studied Every Ecommerce Offer So You Don’t Have To.txt
questions.quote: If AOV is >$100, use Dollar Off (e.g., $25 off).
answer_points: If AOV is above $100, use a dollar amount off (e.g. $25 off)
If AOV is below $100, use a percentage off (e.g. 20% off)

questions.q: Is there a way to lift pop-up sign-ups without making my welcome discount bigger?
questions.source: 03-OFF-offers/I Studied Every Ecommerce Offer So You Don’t Have To.txt
questions.quote: Just by offering the exact same thing, but hiding the offer and saying it's a mystery
answer_points: Show the same discount (e.g. 10%) as a hidden "mystery offer" in a full-width pop-up
Reported around 15% opt-in, roughly doubling sign-up conversion

questions.q: Which Shopify sales figure should I treat as the actual cash collected when I work out profit?
questions.source: 06-MEA-measurement/What Metrics Matter In The Shopify Analytics Dashboard.txt
questions.quote: understand cash collected within the business is to take net sales and add it to shipping charges
answer_points: Cash collected = net sales + shipping charges
Not total sales (includes tax, a flow-through) and not gross sales (ignores discounts and returns)

questions.q: What's a normal drop-off between add to cart, reaching checkout and purchase in Shopify's funnel report?
questions.source: 06-MEA-measurement/What Metrics Matter In The Shopify Analytics Dashboard.txt
questions.quote: for every four ad to cards you should expect two reach checkouts and one purchase
answer_points: A 4:2:1 ratio (4 add-to-carts : 2 reached checkout : 1 purchase) is a general average
Aim to move it toward 2:1:1, with very little drop between checkout and purchase

questions.q: Shopify shows a lot more sessions than GA4, and Shopify's conversion rate tanked one day. Which one do I trust?
questions.source: 06-MEA-measurement/What Metrics Matter In The Shopify Analytics Dashboard.txt
questions.quote: Google analytics does a much better job at not counting bot traffic
answer_points: Shopify keeps bot traffic, so its sessions run higher and its conversion rate can be wrong (a dip may just be a bot spike)
GA4 filters bots, so its session count is lower; check both before reacting

questions.q: I set up Meta's CAPI Gateway expecting it to recover the conversions ad blockers hide. Will it?
questions.source: 06-MEA-measurement/Facebook Conversions API gateway tutorial (FB CAPI Gateway a.k.a. Meta CAPI gateway).txt
questions.quote: if an extension blocks this part, it means that this part is also automatically blocked
answer_points: No: the gateway request depends on the browser pixel loading first
If an extension such as Ghostery blocks the pixel, the server-side gateway call is blocked too; true independent server-side tagging is needed

questions.q: Can I use Shopify's returning customer rate to judge how loyal my customers are?
questions.source: 06-MEA-measurement/What Metrics Matter In The Shopify Analytics Dashboard.txt
questions.quote: it's really important to understand that this misleads people enormously to how loyal their customers actually are
answer_points: No: it is the share of orders from existing customers in the selected window, so it swings with new-customer acquisition
It misrepresents cohort loyalty

questions.q: Can I charge for shipping without hurting conversion, or does everything need to ship free?
questions.source: 09-CRO-testing/eCommerce CRO Masterclass 2026_ The Full System.txt
questions.quote: Most people can charge shipping up to about 10% of the average order value of the cart.
answer_points: Shipping charges up to about 10% of AOV have no material impact on conversion
If you give free shipping, put it at a threshold to push AOV up

questions.q: We aren't running any promotions right now. Should the discount code box stay in the cart?
questions.source: 09-CRO-testing/Conversion Rate Optimization Framework Revealed - Step By Step Breakdown.txt
questions.quote: if you don't have active discounts on your site, get rid of the discount box on your cart
answer_points: Remove the discount box when there is no active promotion
Shoppers leave to search Google for codes and abandon (especially older buyers)

questions.q: We only get about 20 orders a month. What kind of A/B test can we realistically run?
questions.source: 09-CRO-testing/CRO as testing and experimentation for DTC ecommerce.txt
questions.quote: You cannot power even a 30% lift in a reasonable window (about 120+ conversions per variant needed).
answer_points: Under 30 orders a month, run no A/B tests at all (cannot power even a 30% lift; ~120+ conversions per variant)
Do qualitative research and apply known best-practice fixes instead

questions.q: We're at roughly 150 orders a month. Should revenue per visitor be the main metric for our A/B tests?
questions.source: 09-CRO-testing/CRO as testing and experimentation for DTC ecommerce.txt
questions.quote: revenue-per-visitor as primary metric (needs about 6x traffic)
answer_points: No: at 30-300 orders a month RPV as the primary metric is not valid (needs about 6x the traffic)
Use micro-conversions (add to cart, begin checkout) as primary with purchase as guardrail, big-swing tests for 20%+ lifts over 2-4 weeks

questions.q: New creative packs in my CBO campaign aren't getting any spend. How much minimum spend should I force on the new ad set, and for how long?
questions.source: 10-MCR-paid-social-creative/The Best AI Ad Creative Strategy for 2026.txt
questions.quote: $50 is going to be like 30% of your budget, cap it at 20% maximum
answer_points: Set the ad set minimum to 1x target CPA
Cap it at 20% of the daily budget if 1x CPA is too large
Remove the minimum after 7 days and let it run

questions.q: A handful of my Meta ads are eating nearly all the budget. Is that normal or a problem?
questions.source: 10-MCR-paid-social-creative/The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.txt
questions.quote: So 4% of ads will hold about 64% of total spend and total revenue generation
answer_points: Normal: Pareto compounds so about 4% of ads take about 64% of spend and revenue
CBO leans into this, but watch over-reliance on a single hero ad

questions.q: We spend about $60k a month on Meta. How much of that should go into producing creative?
questions.source: 10-MCR-paid-social-creative/The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.txt
questions.quote: you want to be thinking of allocating 25% of media budget towards production
answer_points: About 25% of media spend for brands at $30k-$100k a month
Scaling down toward 10% once spend is above $100k a month

questions.q: I have one video sales letter body that converts. How many different openings should I cut for it, and is it worth it?
questions.source: 10-MCR-paid-social-creative/The 7-Part VSL Framework for eCommerce (With Examples).txt
questions.quote: The hook's going to be the biggest component here because 80% of people won't watch past the hook.
answer_points: Test about 3 to 6 hook variations on the same body
About 80% of viewers never get past the hook

questions.q: How do I measure whether our creative team is actually producing winners and not just volume?
questions.source: 10-MCR-paid-social-creative/The ONLY 2 Ad Creative Formats You Need to Scale Facebook Ads.txt
questions.quote: If the creative hit my target and spent more than 5% of the total campaign budget, it is a winner.
answer_points: Creative hit rate = winning ads / total ads launched
A winner spent more than 5% of the campaign budget and hit target CPA
About 5 winners per 100 launched (5%) is a normal hit rate

questions.q: Should my product page copy try to appeal to every visitor who lands on it?
questions.source: 11-ADC-ad-copy-deployment/COPY HACKERS.txt
questions.quote: Write Copy for 20 to 35% of Your Visitors – Not 100% of Them
answer_points: Write for a specific qualified segment of about 20-35% of visitors, not 100%
Copy neutralised to suit everyone loses its pull

questions.q: I'm scraping competitors' short videos to learn which hooks work. Which videos should I drop before analysing them?
questions.source: 11-ADC-ad-copy-deployment/Claude + Sandcastles = Irresistible Hooks.txt
questions.quote: any video with below a 2% engagement rate, that's a high performer, has paid spend behind it
answer_points: Exclude high-view videos with engagement below about 2% (likely paid brand deals inflating views)
Also drop personal vlogs so only genuine hook data remains

questions.q: What reading level should my ad copy be written at?
questions.source: 11-ADC-ad-copy-deployment/8 Hour Copywriting Course For Beginners.txt
questions.quote: you don't want to write copy that's any more complicated than a third grade
answer_points: No more complicated than a third-grade reading level
The simplest copy is the best copy

questions.q: Is there a quick test I can run on each line of my ad copy to see if it is any good?
questions.source: 11-ADC-ad-copy-deployment/Learn Copywriting in 76 Minutes – Harry Dry.txt
questions.quote: Can I visualize it? Can I falsify it? Can nobody else say this?
answer_points: Three tests per line: can I visualise it, can I falsify it, could nobody else say it
Three nos means rubbish; three yeses means you are on to something

questions.q: When should my win-back flow start for customers who have gone quiet?
questions.source: 14-EML-email-lifecycle/Ecommerce Email Marketing 2025.txt
questions.quote: Winback (3 emails deployed at 2x the average order interval)
answer_points: Trigger at twice the average time between orders
Three emails in the flow

questions.q: My campaign open rates sit around 35%. Is that a deliverability problem, and who should I be sending to?
questions.source: 14-EML-email-lifecycle/Ecommerce Email Marketing 2025.txt
questions.quote: if you're getting sub 40% opens you are likely getting higher promotions Tab and spam inbox placement
answer_points: Under 40% opens signals promotions-tab and spam placement (poor sender reputation)
Send to a tight engaged segment (e.g. 30-day) and widen to 60/90/120 days only as opens climb toward 50%

questions.q: Who should I exclude from SMS blasts? Do I need complicated segments?
questions.source: 14-EML-email-lifecycle/How to Create a SMS Marketing Strategy For $10M Shopify Brands.txt
questions.quote: users who have received 15+ texts with zero clicks
answer_points: Broadcast to the whole SMS list
Suppress only chronically unengaged subscribers: 15+ texts received with zero clicks

questions.q: When someone gives us their phone number, how quickly should our first text go out?
questions.source: 14-EML-email-lifecycle/If I Started SMS Marketing in 2026, I_d Do This.txt
questions.quote: Wait 5 minutes after they've opted into your funnel before texting them.
answer_points: Wait about 5 minutes after opt-in so it feels like a real person
Keep messages short (under about 80 characters)

questions.q: How soon after sign-up does my welcome flow need to do most of its work?
questions.source: 14-EML-email-lifecycle/2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).txt
questions.quote: The critical purchase window for welcome flows: the first 72 hours (with day zero driving the highest conversion volume)
answer_points: The first 72 hours are the critical purchase window
Day zero converts the most, so front-load the flow (two emails on day zero)

questions.q: When I filter TikTok Shop products in Kalodata, what monthly revenue range finds winners that aren't already saturated?
questions.source: 01-PRD-product-research/This Product Research Method Made Me $2.3M Dropshipping (LIVE HUNTING).txt
questions.quote: Revenue Range = $33k to $97k (to avoid hyper-competitive $300k+ products)
answer_points: Last 30 days, revenue $33k-$97k (avoid $300k+ products)
Count video revenue only (exclude live) and sort lowest to highest to catch early breakouts

questions.q: In an ad spy tool, which filters show that a product is actually profitable before I copy it?
questions.source: 01-PRD-product-research/Transcript of the product research method that made me $670k.txt
questions.quote: Runtime, we're going to do minimum 14 days. And for the channels, we're going to do Facebook
answer_points: Ads running at least 14 days
Brand has more than 50 active ads
Facebook channel (older, easier-to-sell audience)

questions.q: How do I quickly tell whether a product idea is a real market or just something I'm passionate about?
questions.source: 02-AVT-avatars/EXACTLY how I do market research for new products.txt
questions.quote: we call it the labor of love you may love it but it's not a profitable business
answer_points: Place the idea on a price vs number-of-customers matrix
Low price and few customers is a "labor of love" quadrant: discard it

questions.q: How much time should I put into manual customer research before writing ads, and where should it go?
questions.source: 02-AVT-avatars/How I Find Avatars That Scale Facebook Ads to $10k_day.txt
questions.quote: Then we're going to spend one hour doing research and we're going to divide that into two phases.
answer_points: One hour in total, split into two 30-minute phases
First forums such as Reddit (search problem statements as the avatar), then Amazon reviews; paste verbatim language

questions.q: For our brand's YouTube channel, how many videos should stay on our core niche versus go broader?
questions.source: 04-BRD-brand/Building a brand, but it’s on easy mode instead.txt
questions.quote: I would say if you do like four like 3 to one four to one in terms of your Longs
answer_points: About 3:1 or 4:1 niche to broad for long-form videos
One wider video for every three or four on-topic ones

questions.q: Is a made-up word that means nothing a good name for my new product?
questions.source: 04-BRD-brand/Positioning_ The Battle for Your Mind_ The Battle for Your Mind (1).txt
questions.quote: Only when you are first in the mind with an absolutely new product
answer_points: Only if you are first in the mind with an absolutely new product that millions will want
Otherwise a coined, meaningless name is dangerous; pick a name that says something

questions.q: My Shopify Payments verification is stuck. I signed up using the short version of my name — could that be it?
questions.source: 05-SET-store-setup/The OFFICIAL Shopify 2026 Tutorial.txt
questions.quote: You'll need to make sure everything matches your governmentissued documents exactly.
answer_points: Legal name, date of birth, tax ID and address must match government ID exactly (e.g. Robert, not Rob)
A mismatch causes verification holds

questions.q: My calculated shipping rates come out lower than what the carrier actually charges me. What did I miss in setup?
questions.source: 05-SET-store-setup/The OFFICIAL Shopify 2026 Tutorial.txt
questions.quote: once you add the box, packing materials, bubble wrap, all of that, it weighs more
answer_points: Set the default package (empty box) weight in the shipping profile
Otherwise calculated rates use product weight only and undercharge

questions.q: I'm adding defer/async to all the scripts in theme.liquid to speed the store up. Is there anything I shouldn't defer?
questions.source: 08-SPD-speed/Page speed.txt
questions.quote: tracking pixels those should not be defered as doing so might mess up the data
answer_points: Defer or async non-essential app scripts
Do not defer tracking pixels, or the collected data can break

questions.q: When I resize product images for speed, what pixel dimensions should I export them at?
questions.source: 08-SPD-speed/WordPress Speed Optimization_ Improve Your Website Performance & Make It Faster (Step-By-Step).txt
questions.quote: my recommendation here is to go down to 2x the rendered size
answer_points: Export at 2x the rendered size so retina screens stay sharp
Not the original file and not exactly the rendered size; use AVIF/WebP

questions.q: I want Standard Shopping and Search to get priority in Google Ads but keep Performance Max running as a backup. How do I set that up?
questions.source: 12-GAD-google-ads/The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.txt
questions.quote: setting PMax ROAS targets much higher than manual campaigns to force budget allocation toward controlled inventory
answer_points: Give PMax a target ROAS much higher than the manual campaigns
That de-prioritises PMax so it only acts as a catch-all safety net

questions.q: Google Ads shows the last three days as a disaster. Should I start changing bids and budgets?
questions.source: 12-GAD-google-ads/How To Fix An Underperforming Google Ads Account.txt
questions.quote: you pull out a custom column called conversions by conversion time
answer_points: Do not panic: conversions are credited back to the click date, so the last 3-4 days always look poor
Read recent days with the "conversions by conversion time" column (and check against business KPIs like MER)

questions.q: When should we start putting calls to action like "grab our free guide" in our brand's short-form videos?
questions.source: 13-ORG-organic-and-content/How to start brand social media from scratch in 2026.txt
questions.quote: Get traction first. All your videos are getting 5,000
answer_points: No CTAs until videos consistently reach about 5,000+ views
Then use soft CTAs that trade free value (PDF, report) for emails

questions.q: Is it fine to schedule our Reels and TikToks ahead of time with a scheduling app?
questions.source: 13-ORG-organic-and-content/How to start brand social media from scratch in 2026.txt
questions.quote: every single scheduling app, including the ones native to the platforms, hurts the performance
answer_points: No: tests across hundreds of videos showed every scheduler, including native ones, hurts reach
Upload and post manually

questions.q: What filters should I use in Semrush to choose keywords worth targeting with my product and collection pages?
questions.source: 15-SEO-search/Complete Shopify SEO Optimization Masterclass For Beginners in 2025 (full course).txt
questions.quote: Commercial intent (C), Volume >1,000, Keyword Difficulty (KD) <40%, and a Cost Per Click
answer_points: Commercial intent, volume above 1,000 a month, keyword difficulty below 40%
CPC above $1 (shows the keyword makes money)

questions.q: I have a small budget for backlinks. Should it go on guest posts or something else?
questions.source: 15-SEO-search/$40,000,000 Worth of Ecommerce SEO Advice in 11 Minutes.txt
questions.quote: prioritizing "link insertions" (niche edits) on existing high-traffic pages over new guest posts due to lower costs ($100-$400)
answer_points: Prefer link insertions (niche edits) on existing pages that already have traffic and authority
They cost less, about $100-$400, than new guest posts

questions.q: How long should the answer right under each heading on my blog posts be so AI search tools quote it?
questions.source: 16-AEO-answer-and-generative-engines/The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.txt
questions.quote: you want to keep that capsule around 20 to 25 words
answer_points: Put a 20-25 word direct answer immediately under the heading
Keep links out of that answer block

questions.q: Our store runs behind Cloudflare. Could that be stopping ChatGPT from seeing our pages?
questions.source: 16-AEO-answer-and-generative-engines/Learn 80_ of AEO in 19 Minutes.txt
questions.quote: if your site is on Cloudflare, you could be blocking AI crawlers without realizing it
answer_points: Yes: Cloudflare's "instruct AI bot traffic with robots.txt" feature is on by default and can disallow GPTBot
Check yourdomain.com/robots.txt for disallow rules on AI bots

questions.q: We're drowning in 'where is my order' tickets. What's the minimum set of automatic updates that fixes most of them?
questions.source: 17-CXP-post-purchase/E-commerce Customer Delight.txt
questions.quote: three-step automated communication flow that can eliminate up to 80% of "Where Is My Order" (WISMO) tickets
answer_points: Three automated messages: order confirmation with delivery estimate, shipping confirmation with tracking link, out-for-delivery notice
Can remove up to 80% of WISMO tickets

questions.q: How do I set a CAC target from the gross profit a customer brings in?
questions.source: 17-CXP-post-purchase/The Complete E-Commerce Retention Masterclass.txt
questions.quote: CAC target: target LTGP divided by the desired efficiency ratio (with 2 to 3 being the optimal scaling band)
answer_points: CAC target = time-bound lifetime gross profit (e.g. 30/90-day LTGP) / efficiency ratio
A ratio of 2 to 3 is the scaling band; LTGP deducts COGS, delivery, fees and refunds

questions.q: I'm placing my first bulk order from an Alibaba supplier. Should I order exactly the quantity I need?
questions.source: 18-COG-sourcing/What I learnt from sourcing e-commerce products from China.txt
questions.quote: So make sure that you order at least 10% more of what you need.
answer_points: Order at least 10% extra to cover defective units (about 300 bad in a 10k order)
Alternatively pay for a ~$200 third-party inspection

questions.q: My factory keeps printing our logo slightly off position. How should I write the spec so it stops happening?
questions.source: 18-COG-sourcing/How He Makes Millions Sourcing Products From China.txt
questions.quote: just because you tell the factory this is centered doesn't mean they're going to center it properly
answer_points: Never write "centered"; give exact measurements from each edge (e.g. 4 in from top, 2 in from side)
Leave the factory no decisions to make

questions.q: For cheap items, is it smarter to refund and let the customer keep the product than to process the return?
questions.source: 19-WLD-wild-bets/Wild bets folder_ unconventional offer, retention and CX plays for e-commerce owners.txt
questions.quote: 59% of surveyed retailers offered a keep-it policy, up from 26% a year earlier, mostly for items up to $20
answer_points: Keep-it (returnless) refunds are mostly used for items up to about $20
Processing a return can cost roughly 20-65% of the item value

questions.q: Is there a way to use physical mail inside my abandoned cart automation?
questions.source: 19-WLD-wild-bets/Wild bets.txt
questions.quote: triggering a physical letter to be mailed 48 hours after a high-value cart abandonment
answer_points: Programmatic direct mail: a printed letter or postcard triggered by the automation
Sent about 48 hours after a high-value cart is abandoned

questions.q: Does the branded box my product sits in count as COGS? What about the carton we ship it in?
questions.source: 20-FIN-finance-and-accounting/Calculating COGS_ What Ecommerce Businesses Get Wrong.txt
questions.quote: that box is part of the cost of goods sold. But the brown box that it goes into
answer_points: The retail/product box is COGS
The brown outer shipping carton is a shipping (operating) expense, not COGS

questions.q: When a returned item comes back to us, which of those costs can I put into COGS?
questions.source: 20-FIN-finance-and-accounting/Calculating COGS_ What Ecommerce Businesses Get Wrong.txt
questions.quote: the labor and materials used to repackage that returned item to make it sellable again are classified as COGS
answer_points: Shipping the return back is an overhead/operating expense
Labour and materials to repackage or refurbish it into sellable stock are COGS

questions.q: I'm at about $3M a year on roughly 12% margin and can't scale ads myself. How do I afford a really good media buyer?
questions.source: 21-OPS-team-and-management/Helping a $3M_Year E-Commerce Brand Build a Team.txt
questions.quote: you might have to give up a few points of equity to get somebody who's really good
answer_points: The missing capability is media buying; bring in a star rather than learning it slowly
Use equity (a few points) alongside cash so the hire does not eat the whole margin

questions.q: Customers say our hoodies feel thinner than the last batch. How can I prove the factory cut corners?
questions.source: 21-OPS-team-and-management/Complete E-commerce Operations Guide.txt
questions.quote: we cut out the designated amount of size of the fabric we weigh it
answer_points: Specify fabric GSM in the tech pack
Cut a fixed-size swatch and weigh it to prove the supplier used lighter fabric, then get it replaced

questions.q: How can I tell from Amazon's first page of results whether a niche has turned into a price war?
questions.source: 22-AMZ-amazon-marketplace/COMPLETE Amazon FBA Product Research Masterclass.txt
questions.quote: If all Page 1 results are tightly clustered (e.g., $7 to $13), discard the product.
answer_points: Look for a wide price spread on page 1 (e.g. $20, $50, $100)
If results are tightly clustered (e.g. $7-$13), discard the product

questions.q: If I send my own ad traffic to my Amazon listing, do I get anything back from Amazon?
questions.source: 22-AMZ-amazon-marketplace/FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.txt
questions.quote: when you send traffic to your Amazon listing page, they actually give you back around 10% right here
answer_points: Yes, the Brand Referral Bonus (Brand Registry) pays back about 10% on sales from external traffic
Effectively cuts the usual 15% referral fee to about 5%

questions.q: At what chargeback rate does my payment processor start to get nervous?
questions.source: 23-SEC-bot-and-agent-security/Ecommerce Security_ Threats and Best Practices.txt
questions.quote: Most processors flag stores whose chargeback rate is higher than 0.9%. Above 1%, processors can stop accepting cards completely.
answer_points: Above 0.9% chargebacks the store gets flagged
Above 1% processors can stop accepting cards entirely

questions.q: We do maybe 8,000 orders a year. Do we need a formal PCI audit?
questions.source: 23-SEC-bot-and-agent-security/Ecommerce Security_ Threats and Best Practices.txt
questions.quote: Most small ecommerce stores fall into Level 4, which describes stores that process fewer than 20,000 transactions per year.
answer_points: No: under 20,000 transactions a year is PCI DSS Level 4

questions.q: How should I split creative production between cold, problem-aware and bottom-of-funnel ads on Meta?
questions.source: 24-DEP-ad-deployment/How To Make Your Meta Ads Scale.txt
questions.quote: you want 80% of volume to be up in these two stages
answer_points: About 80% of creative volume on unaware and problem-aware stages
10% solution-aware and 10% product/most-aware

questions.q: I exclude every past buyer from my cold Meta campaigns, even people who bought years ago. Is that right?
questions.source: 24-DEP-ad-deployment/How To Scale Meta TOF Campaigns.txt
questions.quote: customers that haven't bought in 2 years? Well, we probably do want a bit of spend on them
answer_points: Exclude existing customers from cold campaigns
But use roughly a 2-year purchase exclusion so lapsed buyers can still be reached

questions.q: How can I get TikTok Shop creators to post every day for a new brand without paying a big flat fee upfront?
questions.source: 99-multi/How Comfrt Made $500M in 3 Years.txt
questions.quote: We'll give you $1,000 a month let's just say or the commission rate 15 20% commission Whichever earns you more
answer_points: Offer a $1,000/month minimum or 15-20% commission, whichever earns the creator more
In exchange for 30 videos (one a day for 30 days)

questions.q: During Black Friday week, how often should I be making budget scaling decisions?
questions.source: 99-multi/Black Friday 2026 Strategy_ Spend, Creative, Offers, Pacing.txt
questions.quote: we typically will scale based on three-day rolling marginal averages
answer_points: Scale on 3-day rolling marginal averages rather than day-to-day results
Write the scaling rules down in advance (pacing sheet)
